key_finding: No government or multilateral primary source publishes a dollar-denominated annual aggregate specifically for booking-layer freight fraud (double brokering, fictitious pickups, identity spoofing). The $500M–$700M figure circulates widely but traces back to industry trade sources — predominantly TIA survey data, not an independently audited statistic. The best available independent proxies are (1) Verisk CargoNet's 2024 reported-incident loss total of ~$455M covering strategic/fraudulent cargo theft (distinct from physical theft), and (2) TIA's April 2025 State of Fraud report which documents 1,611 fraud reports in a 6-month window with 22% of brokerages losing >$200K each period, implying industry-wide losses well above $500M annually but without a stated aggregate. FBI IC3 does not break out freight fraud as a subcategory. DOT OIG tracks individual case restitution, not annual aggregates. NICB covers cargo-theft insurance losses, not booking-layer fraud specifically.

sources_evaluated.key_data: TIA Watchdog recorded 1,611 fraud reports Sep 2024–Feb 2025 (65% increase YoY); 22% of brokerages lost >$200K in that 6-month period; truckload fraud up across all categories. Does NOT state an industry-wide annual aggregate dollar figure.

sources_evaluated.key_data: IC3 2024 report covers $16.6B total internet crime losses. Does NOT break down by industry vertical or freight subcategory. Freight fraud is not a listed crime category.
sources_evaluated.independence_rating: primary-government — but irrelevant; no freight subcategory

sources_evaluated.key_data: Verisk CargoNet: 2025 estimated cargo theft losses $725M; 2024 reported incident value ~$455M. CargoNet includes 'strategic cargo theft' (fraud-initiated incidents) but bundles it with physical theft; does not isolate booking-layer fraud separately.
CargoNet 2025 full-year: $725M estimated losses including strategic fraud; 60% YoY increase. Confirms scale of problem exceeds $500M mark when fraud-type theft is included.
NMFTA cites $6.6B annualized cost of cargo theft (source: truckingresearch.org / ATRI); $35B broader supply-chain crime estimate (NICB). These figures are broader than booking-layer fraud alone.
Grant Thornton article on double brokering discusses legal cases only; contains NO aggregate annual loss figures or methodology.

sources_evaluated.key_data: Carrier411 CEO estimated double-brokering costs $100M/year — far below $500M–$700M. Confirms the $500–700M figure does NOT originate from this source.

FreightWaves analysis finds all large cargo-theft/fraud loss estimates involve extrapolation from reported-incident data (typically 10–15% reporting rate). No primary source for $500–700M identified; ATRI baseline cited as $6B for physical theft only.

traceability_of_500_700M_figure.finding: The $500M–$700M double-brokering-specific figure could not be traced to a verifiable primary source. Search results attribute it variously to 'the Wall Street Journal,' 'a TIA 2023 study,' and 'industry sources' — none of which, upon direct verification, contain this figure as a first-party calculation. The most likely origin is a TIA member survey extrapolation or a vendor-cited estimate that entered circulation without documented methodology. FTV Capital's use of this figure likely reflects the same industry-folklore number.
traceability_of_500_700M_figure.closest_verifiable_proxy: CargoNet/Verisk $455M (2024 reported incidents including strategic fraud) — a reported-incident floor, not a total market estimate

revised_claim_options.revised_claim_text: Verisk CargoNet recorded ~$455M in 2024 cargo theft losses including fraud-initiated (strategic) incidents — a reported floor; with an estimated 10–15% reporting rate, total booking-layer and cargo fraud losses are likely in the $1B–$3B range, though no independently audited aggregate exists.

[ASSUMED-N]: $500M–$700M industry-wide annual freight fraud loss — widely cited but not independently audited; to validate: commission analysis of TIA survey raw data + CargoNet strategic-theft subcategory + FMCSA enforcement restitution totals.

Industry estimates of annual freight fraud losses range from $455M (Verisk CargoNet 2024 reported incidents) to $6.6B (ATRI/NMFTA broader cargo crime) with the booking-layer fraud subcategory unquantified by any government agency.
revised_claim_options.note: This accurately represents the state of knowledge without fabricating a single-point estimate.

reasoning: No government or multilateral source publishes a booking-layer-specific fraud aggregate. The $500–$700M figure is industry folklore — plausible but unaudited. The strongest defensible approach is to cite Verisk CargoNet's $455M (2024 confirmed-incident floor, semi-independent data provider) alongside the NMFTA/ATRI $6.6B broader cargo-crime ceiling, and note that the booking-layer subcategory is not independently quantified. This is more credible than retaining FTV Capital as the source.
